decisions.because: Counterexample (hunt round 4, 2026-10-12): after tick dropped a used lease at the claim's end, a 50 s wall step back and a resend gave the claim a second lease (R26-07: the bound is total per claim); a lift was undone by an 11 min step back without a restart, while ADR-0003 disclaimed that only between restarts. Owner chose option A. Witnesses added after the mutation check (PR #15).

Counterexample on c51cdc9: a peer claim ending at 590 s under a 600 s cap had no lease record; after a 500 s step back and a resend it was enforced again until 605 s past its start. Every enforced peer claim now records its lease end.

ROADMAP item 9: the lease arithmetic moved to common::lease so that Kani proves it for every input (lease::proofs: a resent claim never outlasts its first lease, a record only moves earlier, within FORGET_GRACE a live resend finds its record; calibrated by proof-task.py with three faults). Lease and lift records now share common::lease::kept, so the bound is the same for both by construction. The unit tests stay.

statement: A wall-clock step back smaller than FORGET_GRACE, with or without a restart, neither renews a peer claim's used lease, including a claim whose own end lies within the cap, nor undoes an operator lift: both records live FORGET_GRACE past the claim's end; a larger step back can revive either, and that bound is the same for both.
